title: Keep energy steady
text: Regular meals and gentle movement you enjoy, such as walking or stretching, can be a good fit. A health professional can give you advice for your situation.

title: A walk after dinner
text: A relaxed 20 to 30 minute walk is an easy way to add some movement to your day.

title: Small, regular movement
text: Short walks spread through the day can add up. Choose a pace where you can still hold a conversation.

title: Fill up on vegetables
text: Vegetables add volume to a meal for few calories, which can help it feel more filling.

title: Plan your strength sessions
text: Two or three strength sessions a week with rest days between them is a common starting point.

title: Spread your protein
text: Having some protein at each meal, rather than most of it at dinner, is a common habit among people building strength.

title: Rest and recover
text: Sleep and rest days are part of training. Most adults feel best with 7 to 9 hours of sleep.

title: Fuel around training
text: Having a meal with carbs and protein within a few hours of training is a common habit among active people.

title: Drink around exercise
text: Sipping water before, during and after longer sessions helps you stay comfortable.

title: Warm up first
text: A few minutes of easy movement before training helps your body get ready.

title: Stay active most days
text: Aim for regular movement you enjoy, such as walking, cycling or swimming.

title: Try something new
text: Mixing up activities, like a bike ride, a swim or a dance class, can keep moving fun.

title: Start with a stretch
text: A few minutes of gentle stretching in the morning can help you feel loose and ready for the day.

title: Protein at breakfast
text: Eggs, yoghurt or beans at breakfast can help keep you full until lunch.

title: Stand up and move
text: If you've been sitting for a while, a short walk or a few minutes on your feet makes a nice break.

title: Plan a balanced dinner
text: You still have room in today's target. Vegetables, a protein and some whole grains make an easy, balanced plate.

title: Wind down before bed
text: A regular bedtime and some screen-free time before sleep help many people rest better.

title: Drink water through the day
text: Keep a glass or bottle nearby and sip regularly. Thirst is a good guide for most people.

title: Add colour to your plate
text: Adding a vegetable or a piece of fruit to each meal is a simple way to eat a wider mix of foods.

title: Eat without screens
text: Slowing down and eating away from screens can make it easier to notice when you're comfortably full.
